News.title: Moment secret service agent, 33, arrested with belt undone after ‘masturbating in front of horrified hotel guests’
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a secret service agent is arrested with his belt undone after allegedly masturbating in front of hotel guests.

Newly released footage shows John Spillman, 33, slide down to the floor before desperately clutching at his unbuckled trousers when approached by police in the hotel.



Spillman had been working as part of Donald Trump’s security team at the 2026 PGA Cadillac Championship in Florida at the time of his arrest.

But while off duty, the agent was accused of exposing his genitals in a hotel corridor by other guests, according to police.



Spillman allegedly began inappropriately touching himself in full view of scandalised Hilton Hotel guests.

Cops raced to the hotel and arrested the suspect in a humiliating bust back in May.

Bodycam footage from the local sheriff’s office shows Spillman’s trousers were still undone even as officers bundled him into an elevator and cuffed him.

The agent admitted that he’d had “too much to drink”, according to TMZ.

One horrified woman reportedly told police that Spillman had allegedly stalked her from the lobby up to her sixth floor room.

The guest said she and her pals “immediately entered their rooms” because they were “in fear of their lives”, claim police docs.



She claimed that they saw Spillman “masturbating next to [the] hotel room”, prompting them to call hotel security.

The Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office confirmed Spillman had “committed the offense of indecent exposure”.

Secret Service Chief Richard Macauley said: “The alleged conduct is unacceptable and stands in stark contrast to the professionalism and integrity that I demand of our personnel.”



The agent has been placed on administrative leave pending the outcome of a criminal probe.

He is being held on $1,000 (£738) bond at Turner Guilford Knight correctional center.

Prosecutors are still searching for CCTV footage showing the off-duty agent in the act.

It comes as another American secret service agent is placed on administrative leave after allegedly leaking secret travel plans.

News.title: Teen ‘stabbed housemate, 19, in the heart after luring him into basement with dead mouse ruse to steal money for taxi’
News.content:
'MURDER' SHOCK' Teen ‘stabbed housemate, 19, in the heart after luring him into basement with dead mouse ruse to steal money for taxi’

A TEEN who allegedly stabbed his flatmate to death “lured” him into the basement pretending there was a dead mouse in the toilet, a court heard.

Musa Salih, 19, has been accused of stabbing Harley Purdue repeatedly at their short-term let in Thorold Road, Chatham, on December 2.

Harley, also 19, sustained seven wounds, including a fatal blow to his lung and heart.

Prosecutor Richard Christie KC told Maidstone Crown Court that Salih had instigated the attack to steal money so he could visit his pregnant girlfriend in London.





The court heard how Salih, who had moved into the property just a week beforehand, “lured” Harley into the basement to allegedly commit the heinous assault.

At around 2.40am, Salih allegedly knocked on the attic room door, where Harley was sleeping with his pregnant girlfriend, Hazel Gasden.

Harley reluctantly followed Salih downstairs, wearing only his boxers and wrapped in a blanket, the court was told.

“Musa Salih got Harley Purdue downstairs, claiming there was a dead mouse in the toilet,” Richard told the court.



“This was a ruse to try and lock Harley Purdue in the basement toilet to go and steal his money.”

Hazel then allegedly heard “banging” and her partner crying out for help, claiming he’d been stabbed.

She told the court that she rushed downstairs to find “lots of blood” on the floor and found her boyfriend in a toilet, who said he was losing consciousness.

Hazel, who was three months pregnant, said she scrambled to the kitchen to grab a butcher’s knife to defend herself and Harley.



During this time, Hazel said Salih ran up to the attic room to take Harley’s money.

After going back upstairs, she allegedly caught Salih dragging a “weak” Harley towards the door while holding a knife against his throat.

Hazel kicked him in the head causing him to “fly into the door” and Salih allegedly “tried stabbing her multiple times”, nicking her chin, the court heard.

He then “stumbled” out of the property and fled before returning shortly afterwards to collect his phone and a bag stuffed with around £300 of the stolen cash.

One witness claimed they heard Harley shouting: “Just give it back to me.



“Just give me my stuff and go.”

A knife covered in Harley’s blood was discarded in the alleyway and discovered by cops, who arrived within minutes to carry out a search.

By then, Salih had reportedly reached Bank Street, where he hid in an empty property.

Records show he tried booking two taxis at 2.38am and 2.41am, which were both cancelled, before eventually booking a third at around 2.44am, to take him to Wembley.

The taxi driver reported that Salih’s clothes had been covered in blood and that he had offered to pay the £119.30 fare with blood-stained cash.



At around 11pm, Salih allegedly asked his girlfriend to send over money to pay for a taxi.

She agreed to send £50 but he demanded more, the court heard.

At around 3.24am, Salih received several more messages from his partner.

“You need to go to the hospital if he stabbed you,” she said.

Another message said: “You promised me. I told you to leave there. What am I going to do? I’m going to lose you and my baby.”



At 4.55am, she said: “I just wish that you could have stayed there and that you could have proved it was self-defence.”

Salih is alleged to have changed his outfit at a friend’s home in London before heading to his mum’s house, where he was arrested on December 2.

Further analysis of Salih’s phone revealed he had consulted ChatGPT about legal advice and a serious incident in Chatham.

He asked whether people could be put on remand for self-defence, what the sentence for manslaughter was, and whether the person involved in a stabbing in Chatham was still alive.

He also asked whether someone with a Portuguese passport could get to Ethiopia.



Salih gave multiple accounts of the attack in the hours after the killing, claiming he had fought back after Harley “flipped” and was being “abusive”.

However, the prosecutor said Salih gave no comment during the police interview.

In an interview recorded in the aftermath, and played to the court, Hazel said she had a “gut-wrenching” feeling something wasn’t right downstairs.

As she went down to the basement, Hazel said Harley told her not to go any further as Salih was “hiding behind the fridge and going to stab her”.

She said: “I wasn’t just going to watch my boyfriend be stabbed, so my reaction was to stab the boy back.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

She added that the attack had been so unexpected and that Salih had looked “so normal”.

The trial, presided over by Judge Oliver Saxby KC, continues.

News.title: Miliband’s sanctions on Israel praised by October 7 terror attackers HAMAS as ‘a step in the right direction’
News.content:
TERROR group Hamas has applauded Ed Miliband’s sanctions on Israel as a “step in the right direction”.

The fanatics behind the October 7 atrocity also praised the Foreign Secretary for claiming Israeli “settler terrorists” are guilty of ethnic cleansing of Palestinians in the West Bank.



And state media in Iran has hailed Mr Miliband’s sanctions as a step towards “the end of Israel”.

On Tuesday, Mr Miliband announced Britain will ban imports from illegal settlements in the West Bank.



Eleven nations joined the UK in taking the action.

Basem Naim, a senior member of Hamas’ political bureau, said: “Sanctions by Britain and other countries, and the foreign minister’s use of the term ‘ethnic cleansing’, are important steps in the right direction — but they are not enough.



“What is needed to achieve peace in Palestine and beyond is the immediate implementation of the relevant international resolutions and the prosecution of war criminals in Israel in a manner similar to the Nazi trials at Nuremberg.”

Hamas, which governs Gaza, is classed in the UK as a terror group.

The October 7 attacks in Israel in 2023 killed 1,200 people.

Richard Tice, deputy leader of Reform UK, said: “Hamas praises their puppet Miliband. He should resign. He has made Jews less safe.”



Mr Miliband, who is Jewish, is the first British minister to call the occupation of Palestinian territory unlawful.

Israel called his words “lies” and announced measures such as shutting Britain’s consulate in Jerusalem.

News.title: Never mind Israel, what will you do about the hordes of illegal settlers in THE UK Mr Miliband?
News.content:
YOU would be hard pushed to find anyone in Britain who is more wrong about more things more often than Ed Miliband.

For the past two years he has been busy being wrong about climate change and Net Zero, insisting on impoverishing our nation to appease the weather gods and his own eco-hysteria.



Now, as our new Foreign Secretary, Mr Miliband has a whole new mission to be wrong about stuff going on in other countries too.

To that end, he chose as his first major foreign policy announcement to impose sanctions on Israel, one of Britain’s staunchest allies.



According to the Foreign Secretary, the biggest moral issue in the world that Britain must confront is not the myriad human rights atrocities taking place across the world in China, Sudan, Iran, Yemen, Afghanistan or Somalia, where thousands of innocent civilians are being slaughtered, systematically starved, tortured and even forcibly sterilised.

No, apparently the No1 ethical concern for HM Government is the violence committed by a small number of Israeli settlers in the West Bank.



Mr Miliband accused the Israeli government of “turning a blind eye” to the violence and carrying out “ethnic cleansing”, which is the deliberate policy of forcing or intimidating an ethnic or religious civilian population out of their homeland and then replacing that population with new settlers.

What a shame Mr Miliband and, indeed, the Prime Minister who appointed him, don’t share those exact same concerns about the invaders and settler violence in our own country.

Back here in Britain, thousands of miles from the Middle East, our own Government is busy turning a blind eye to the threat to British people and our way of life posed by the tens of thousands of illegal migrants walking Britain’s streets.

It no longer matters whether you live in an inner city, in bustling Portsmouth on the south coast or in the leafy village of Piddington in rural Oxfordshire, this menace is coming to everyone’s door soon.



And while the Government wants to turn a blind eye to this threat, the people of Britain have made it abundantly clear that they are not willing to take that risk any more.

This weekend we saw hundreds of protesters in Portsmouth — some organised and balaclava-clad but many of them just concerned locals — block the roads to stop coaches carrying 120 illegal migrants who had arrived from Normandy on a mega-dinghy.

Meanwhile, miles away in Piddington, the quiet village’s 350 residents learned that an expected influx of 1,250 illegal boat migrants due to be housed on a nearby Ministry of Defence site could now rise to 3,500 or more young men of fighting age from overseas.

That’s ten times the number of local residents.

How is what is happening in Piddington not the same as what Ed Miliband claims is happening in the West Bank?



Is this not the very arrival of foreign settlers with no claim to the land?

Sure, no one is physically forcing villagers to up sticks and sell — not that anyone would want to buy their homes any more given their new nuisance neighbours.

But if a group of foreign arrivals numbering ten times the local population suddenly arrives on your doorstep without your agreement, what also can you call it but an invasion and occupation?



No wonder the good folk of Piddington are planning to go ahead next week with their planned referendum on whether to formally secede from the United Kingdom so the British Government cannot impose these thousands of migrant men on them.

The symbolic vote won’t have any legal standing but it will send a clear message that they do not consent to this outrage.

And the fact it takes place on Tuesday — Battle of Britain Day, marking the 86th anniversary of the air conflict — only adds to its poignancy.

Tuesday also happens to be the UN’s International Day of Democracy — yet another reminder that no one in Britain ever voted to open our borders to anyone and everyone who is willing to pay people smugglers for a place on a dinghy to get here.

Piddington won’t be the first village to experience what is, to all intents and purposes, forced ethnic cleansing under Andy Burnham’s policy of sharing out illegal migrants across the country.



Some 200,000 illegal arrivals since 2018 are still living in the UK, at our expense, and no one expects them to be deported any time ever.

They are walking freely on our streets and far too many of them are committing violent crimes.

There have been at least seven killings of Brits by illegal arrivals in recent years, including hotel worker Rhiannon Whyte, dog walker Wayne Broadhurst and restaurateur Gurvinder Singh Johal, as well as many, many more cases of sexual assaults and rapes of women and children.

Yet Ed Miliband is more concerned with what is happening to Palestinians 2,200 miles away than protecting British people in a village just a short drive up the M40 from Westminster.

The truth is that hardly anyone wants these migrants. Not our villages, not our towns, not our cities.



We don’t want them in hotels or in hostels, not in army barracks or in bedsits. We don’t want them here at all.

And if we do have to have them here, most people would prefer them to be detained behind lock and key so they cannot pose a threat to our safety or to our way of life.

Ed Miliband insisted this week that economic sanctions on Israel were vital to preserve the chance of a two-state solution in the Middle East.

And once again Mr Wrong About Everything got his facts and his priorities wrong.

He — and Andy Burnham — should be worrying more about protecting British people from the hordes of invaders to our own territory.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

At the rate things are going, we might need a two-state solution here in Britain.

I don’t know about you but, in that referendum, I’m voting with Piddington.

News.title: An almighty bang, choking flames & a horror movie scream I’ll never forget… my heart-stopping 84th floor escape on 9/11
News.content:
IT only takes a clock clicking 9.11am and Janice Brooks is jolted back inside the World Trade Center as the hijacked plane struck.

As if watching some barely believable disaster movie, the survivor will vividly relive the “almighty thud”, the 1,362ft South Tower swaying precariously and the blood-curdling screams of those inside.





Recalling the atrocity, which killed 2,753 innocent victims, Janice, 66, tells me: “It’s like the universe is ­conspiring to never let me forget — as if I could. I can close my eyes and be back there in an instant.”

As the 25th anniversary of history’s deadliest terror attack approached, Janice was plagued by nightmares.

Miraculously, she escaped the South Tower from close to the plane’s impact point.

But the fact 61 of her work colleagues did not make it remains an enduring sadness that compels her to share her story.

It was a gloriously sunny autumn day in the Big Apple — Tuesday, ­September 11, 2001 — and Janice had arrived at her desk at Euro Brokers on the 84th floor of the South Tower at 7.30am.

The executive assistant had already been for an early morning jog along the Hudson River, savouring the days after landing her dream job.

Born in Stepney, East London, Janice — the eldest of five children with a lorry driver dad and an office cleaner mum — had made a life-changing decision on reaching 40.

She revealed: “I had one of those, ‘What am I doing with my life?’ moments. I thought, ‘I work for an American company. I love America. Why not go and work there?’





“So on August 23, 2001, I arrived in New York to begin the biggest adventure of my life.”

Divorcee Janice produces a photo taken of herself on September 7, 2001, at the Top Of The World observatory on the roof of the South Tower, also known as 2 World Trade Center.

Smiling broadly as the setting sun dipped below the Manhattan skyline, her excitement was unmistakable.

Just over three days later, Janice’s world changed for ever.

At 8.46am on 9/11, American Airlines Flight 11 — carrying 92 passengers and crew — emerged from blue skies with crazed al-Qaeda hijackers at the controls and smashed into the World Trade Center’s North Tower.

In the neighbouring skyscraper, Janice remained unruffled.

“I was at my desk, eating breakfast, when I heard a loud bang,” she recalls.

“At the time, New York was experiencing a construction boom so there were often big bangs.”

Janice carried on sending emails for another five minutes. Then, a man boomed at the top of his voice: “Everybody out!”

She called Euro Brokers’ London office and spoke to then-UK managing director Robin Clark, who screamed: “F***ing hell, Janice, a plane’s gone into the building, get the f*** out of there.”



Janice said: “Robin was watching on telly 3,500 miles away and I had no clue what was happening 200 yards behind me.”

She grabbed her Louis Vuitton handbag and ran as staff began ­evacuating down the stairs.

But Janice said there was no panic: “The chit-chat around me was what people had done at the weekend,” she recalls.

Descending from the 84th floor, Janice’s heels were cumbersome so she put them in her bag and ­continued barefoot.

When she reached the 72nd floor, there were repeated announcements from the building’s security that it was safe and staff should return to their offices. Joining a group including some ­fellow Euro Brokers employees, she began climbing the stairs again.

It was now 9.03am and they entered a corridor between stairwells, which Janice estimates was between the 76th and 78th floors.

As the world watched on live TV, United Airlines Flight 175 carrying 65 people wheeled through the ­Manhattan sky at 540mph and rammed into the second tower.

Tilting at an angle, the fuel-laden jet, piloted by terrorists, carved a gaping hole from the 77th to the 85th floors. Janet believes she and her fellow staff members were below the plane’s right wing.



She remembers: “There was an almighty thud and the tower began to sway. The lights flashed on and off and parts of the ceiling fell in.

“There was dust and debris ­everywhere. After a while, the building seemed to shudder and stand still. The lights flickered and came back on.”

Janice’s group headed back to the stairwell, but it had ­“disappeared”, replaced by “darkness and flames”.

She says: “Just as we’re starting to digest that, we heard one of those horror story screams that live in your head for ever.” A traumatised woman was trapped behind another door.

Led by a man in a white shirt, ­Janice and others cleared away rubble and prised it open.

A group of dazed people stumbled through, led by a badly injured woman.

Janet explains: “She was cut almost neatly from her shoulder to her elbow. Her skin and muscle were flapping down and I could see the bone. As she moved, blood was going everywhere. Then a guy came through with a big piece of glass sticking out of his chest, followed by a guy with his back covered in blood.”

Finally came the screaming woman. Janice adds: “She had long, dark hair and was crying, ‘I can’t see’.



“She had a cut on her forehead and the blood was dribbling down into her eyes.”

One of the men in the group had his gym bag with him and fashioned the first woman a splint from a T-shirt, before cleaning the blood from the second.

Then an explosion from the other tower blew all the windows in. Miraculously, the terrified group found another door. After wrestling it open, they set off down the stairs. Still barefoot and clutching her handbag, Janet soon began to notice blood oozing through her toes.

She recalls: “I was going to scream, but then realised it was blood from the lady with the gashed arm who also appeared to have lost half her foot.”

The well-lit stairwell was ­littered with exposed wires and debris, with a broken pipe causing water to gush down the steps.

After descending a few more flights, Janice noticed her shirt was covered in blood. In shock, she stood stock still until colleague Bob Mahon grabbed her by the elbows and said: “It’s not your blood. We have to get out of here, we have to keep going.”

The group continued down the stairs, with Bob giving the woman with the gashed arm a piggyback for the last few flights.

Finally, they made it to ground level, where a burly policeman yelled: “Keep your heads down, don’t look up.”



Janice and Bob headed for her 17th-floor apartment, which was just ten minutes’ walk away. It was 9.43am.

For the first time, she looked back at the tower.

“Where our floor should have been, there was this huge gaping hole with flames coming out,” she recalls.

After helping her home, Bob left and Janice made a cup of tea before switching on the TV. That is when she realised for the first time she had been in the midst of a terror attack.

Soon after, she heard a giant ­rumbling noise. A reporter on TV shouted: “The tower’s down!”

It was 9.59am and the South Tower Janice had fled a short time before had crumpled like a house of cards.

She remembers: “The noise was incredible. The windows hummed, crockery in the dishwasher rattled and the lights went out.

“Clouds of dust billowed around my windows and then it went black.”

At 10.28am, the North Tower came crashing down. Janice says: “I was rocking backwards and forward on my sofa, thinking I was going to die.”

Eventually, she fled her home to stay with a friend in an outer New York suburb. Astonishingly, Janice was back at work the next day in a temporary office manning her company’s help desk.



It is only now, after more than an hour of recounting her story, that this remarkable woman breaks down in tears as she recalls how 61 of her 300 Euro Brokers colleagues perished.

Sobbing, Janice tells me: “To my utter shame, I only went to 23 of their funerals.

“I think it’s the one thing I’ll take to the grave, that these people died and I didn’t make the effort to go to more funerals than I did.”

Janice worked in New York for another five years before returning to London to continue her City career.

She went through therapy, found strength in her Christian beliefs and “made the best of life”.

Today, we are talking in her Norfolk cottage near Diss, where red admiral butterflies flutter though a lilac-filled garden.

She gains solace from her work with charity Since 9/11, reliving her experiences for school children to build hope from tragedy.

Janet roots around in her bedroom and emerges with the Louis Vuitton bag she clutched as she fled the tower — and a vial of dust she scooped up from her flat on 9/11.

“The bag still has the stains on it from that day,” she reveals. “I need to keep them there to remind me of it.”

Today, on the harrowing anniversary of the atrocity, Janice will be at Ground Zero in New York paying quiet respect to the 9/11 victims.



Staring out over the tranquil ­Norfolk landscape, she tells me: “I still have bad days.

“If I feel black moods coming, I go out to the garden, let my hands touch the soil and it goes.”

News.title: Moment RAF chopper stuns guests at £2k-a-night hotel by landing on lawn before crew nip in to collect CAKE
News.content:
FLAPJACK HAWK DOWN Moment RAF chopper stuns guests at £2k-a-night hotel by landing on lawn before crew nip in to collect CAKE

AN RAF Chinook ­ helicopter crew landed in the grounds of a £2,000-a-night hotel — and left with cakes and treats.

Guests were stunned when the 98ft chopper thundered on to the castle lawns of the Cameron House Hotel on the shores of Loch Lomond.



An airman in his flight helmet then hot-footed inside — emerging minutes later clutching bags of cake after hotel bosses learnt it was the retiring pilot’s birthday.

Others then briefly joined him inside the hotel at the invitation of the management.



A spokesman for the five-star resort told The Sun: “We often accommodate military and emergency service training landings.

“On learning the flight coincided with the pilot’s birthday, and was also their final flight before retirement, our team welcomed the crew with complimentary refreshments to mark the milestone.”



After its birthday cake pitstop, the chopper took off without even having shut off its engines.

A witness said: “They didn’t hang around. It was a case of have your cake and beat it!

“We couldn’t believe it. It’s not every day you see a Chinook landing on a hotel lawn.”

An RAF source thanked the hotel last night and said: “It is great to see the public backing our armed forces. The hotel agreed to let us land and then offered the crew some afternoon snacks. It is a little gesture but great for morale.”



The pilots were part of 28 Squadron based at the RAF’s Leuchars Station, 70 miles away.

It is an operational conversion unit where pilots learn how to fly Chinooks.

Top brass were terrified the RAF would be accused of wasting money.



They explained that the chopper had made its landing so that they could switch the pilot in the captain’s seat.

The RAF source told The Sun: “The ­Chinook landed as part of an essential navigation training exercise for student aircrew.

“It was scheduled to allow a captaincy change.”

Rotating pilots is a cost-saving measure to give aircrew enough hours at the controls to legally be allowed to fly, while cutting the total number of flights.

An official RAF source said: “Hotel staff unexpectedly provided food to the crew during the stop.



“They didn’t request it and it was not part of the planned activity.”

News.title: Lindsay Clancy could get massive payout with ‘Son of Sam’ law loophole – what it means if killer mom sells story
News.content:
LINDSAY Clancy could rake in big bucks by selling her story despite efforts to stop criminals from cashing in on their crimes.

The 36-year-old former nurse could potentially land lucrative book, TV or documentary deals after her sensational case ended in a mistrial.



Clancy strangled her children, Cora, five, Dawson, three, and eight-month-old Callan with exercise bands on January 24, 2023, before attempting to take her own life by cutting herself and jumping from a second-floor window, leaving her paralyzed.

Her defense argued she was suffering from postpartum psychosis and could not appreciate the wrongfulness of her actions, while prosecutors maintained she was depressed but knew right from wrong.



The case sparked a huge debate over postpartum mental illness and how it is treated by the criminal justice system, but ended in a mistrial after jurors failed to reach a unanimous verdict.

But Clancy’s legal battle is far from over, with the original murder charges still pending and prosecutors yet to announce whether they will put her on trial again.

Her attorney Kevin Reddington has now filed a motion asking Judge William Sullivan to acquit her, while also preparing to argue that a second trial should be barred on double jeopardy grounds.

The case is due back before Plymouth Superior Court on September 29.

Now, The U.S. Sun can reveal there is currently no specific “Son of Sam” law in Massachusetts that could potentially stop Clancy profiting from the notoriety surrounding the case.

Such laws exist in various forms elsewhere in the US and are designed to prevent offenders from cashing in on their crimes through book, television, movie and other media deals.



They take their name from New York serial killer David Berkowitz, whose 1970s murder spree sparked fears he could make money by selling his story.

With no specific crime-profits law currently in force in Massachusetts, she could potentially be paid for a tell-all book, television interview, documentary or other project if she ever decides to tell her story.

Her account could prove valuable because she did not take the stand during her trial and has never given a full first-person account of what she remembers about the day she killed her children.



Instead, jurors heard about her state of mind through medical records, text messages, interviews, doctors and psychiatric experts.

They also examined her prescription pills and heard extensive evidence about the medications she was prescribed before the killings.

Her defense said she heard a commanding voice telling her to kill her children and herself, while prosecutors argued she deliberately planned the killings after sending her husband Patrick out to collect medication and takeout.

Publishers could also potentially pursue a memoir covering her mental health struggles, psychiatric treatment, the killings and the years she has spent hospitalized since.

Documentary and podcast producers could seek exclusive access, while there could eventually be interest in rights connected to her life story for a scripted television series or movie.



Interest in the case has continued since the mistrial, with Reddington embarking on a media blitz and appearing on several television news stations to discuss the trial and his client.

Jurors have also begun speaking publicly, revealing they were split 11-1 in favor of finding Clancy not guilty by reason of lack of criminal responsibility.

They have described tense deliberations involving the lone holdout who refused to acquit her.



While many are speaking out about the case, Clancy herself has remained silent.

Reddington said this week that she is still vulnerable and under “24/7, one-on-one suicide watch”.

Clancy has remained in psychiatric care since the killings and continues to be held at Tewksbury Hospital.

There is no suggestion Clancy has received, sought or is currently negotiating any media offers, and Reddington has not publicly suggested she intends to profit from the case.

Massachusetts lawmakers have repeatedly tried to change the law to address people making money from the notoriety surrounding crimes.



Republican state Rep. Bradley H. Jones Jr. introduced the latest proposal, known as H.1789, in January 2025.

It would cover people who have been charged or convicted, as well as those who have admitted committing a crime, meaning it could potentially apply to someone in Clancy’s position.

The proposal would also cover defendants found not guilty by reason of insanity.

But the bill was shelved for further study in March 2026 and has not become law.

Similar proposals have been introduced in Massachusetts for more than a decade without making it onto the books.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Interest in the case shows no sign of fading.

A GoFundMe for Clancy’s parents, Mike and Paula Musgrove, has already raised more than $1.2 million to help ease the financial burden of spending more than three years supporting their daughter.

News.title: Mum charged with murder of 17-month-old daughter after tot found dead at home with multiple serious injuries
News.content:
BABY HORROR Mum charged with murder of 17-month-old daughter after tot found dead at home with multiple serious injuries

A MUM has been charged with the murder of her 17-month old daughter after the baby was found with multiple severe wounds.

Faiza Hassan is accused of murdering her daughter while the tot’s grandmother was charged with allowing the death of a child.

Officers were called to an address on Castle Hill, Dudley, by paramedics at around 5.20pm on April 9, 2023.

The defendant’s daughter was pronounced dead later the same day.





A post-mortem examination established that she had died after suffering a number of injuries, police said.

Faiza Hassan was also charged with cruelty to the girl and another child.

Her mother, Sahra Hassan, 61, faces charges of allowing the death of the 17-month-old and cruelty to her.

The West Midlands force, which did not name the deceased child, said in a statement: “Following a thorough investigation, her mother and grandmother have now been charged with multiple offences.

“As well as murder, Faiza Hassan, of Dudley, faces eight charges of wounding with intent, between 1 November 2022 and 9 April 2023.

“She is also accused of cruelty to the girl and cruelty to another child, between the same dates.

“Faiza Hassan’s mother, Sahra Hassan, aged 61, of Walsall, is accused of allowing the death of the 17-month-old, and cruelty to her between the same dates.”

Both women appeared before the Recorder of Wolverhampton and are due to appear in court again on October 9.



Faiza was remanded in custody and Sahra was conditionally bailed.

A spokesperson for the police said: “We were called to an address on Castle Hill by paramedics at around 5.20pm on 9 April 2023.

“Sadly, the girl was pronounced dead later that day. A post-mortem established that she had died after suffering a number of injuries.

“Following a thorough investigation, her mother and grandmother have now been charged with multiple offences.

“As well as murder, Faiza Hassan, of Dudley, faces eight charges of wounding with intent, between 1 November 2022 and 9 April 2023.”



This comes just days after two men and two women were arrested after a three-month-old baby died in woodland while camping with her family.

Two men aged 42 and 18, and two women aged 30 and 20, were arrested on suspicion of murder.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The makeshift campsite where the girl died was set up in a woodland clearing to the side of a fishing lake.

At the site there was evidence of a campfire and a lot of litter including children’s clothing, a toy car and the holdall for a two-man Halfords pop up tent.

News.title: 'Tourism tax means locals won't shoulder unfair cost', Wembley Stadium local council leader says
News.content:
'Tourism tax means locals won't shoulder unfair cost', Wembley Stadium local council leader says

EXCLUSIVE: A tourism levy has been praised by the leader of Brent Council, which covers Wembley Stadium, who said it would mean 'real benefits to our businesses and local economy' but also help bring visitors back

View 3 Images The leader of the Brent Council said a tourism levy would be a 'pro-growth measure' (Image: Getty Images)

The local leader of the authority that covers Wembley Stadium has welcomed a new tourism tax and called the plans a "pro-growth measure".

‌



The Government, on Thursday, announced plans to give regional mayors greater economic power and the ability to implement a levy on overnight stays. Local leaders will set the fee as a percentage of the cost of accommodation, rather than a flat rate, which ministers argue will protect budget trips.

‌



The levy will have no upper limit, though Government sources said mayors are unlikely to make it too expensive. Brent Council, home to Wembley Stadium and Wembley Arena, last year proposed a motion to implement a visitors levy. The council leader has welcomed today's announcement and said it could help "give us more to invest back into the area".

‌



View 3 Images Councillor Muhammed Butt praised the tourism levy announcement (Image: Muhammed Butt/LinkedIn )

Similar schemes already exist in Europe, the US and Canada to help fund local services and attractions. Mayors will decide how to spend the revenue raised from the fee rather than money being funnelled back into the Treasury.

Brent Council leader Cllr Muhammed Butt told the Mirror a visitor levy would help the authority as large-scale event in the borough "brings very real pressures". Wembley Stadium welcomed more than 2.5million fans this summer alone for concerts from Harry Styles, The Weekend and Luke Combs. England's national football stadium will also host the final of the 2028 Euro's final and a NFL match this October.

‌



Cllr Butt said: "We are immensely proud to be home to Wembley Stadium and Arena and to host some of the biggest sporting and music events in the world. There are few better sights for me than seeing Wembley packed, with families and fans enjoying themselves and people travelling from across the country and around the world to visit our borough. These events are a huge part of what makes Brent such a special place and bring real benefits to our businesses and local economy.

View 3 Images Fans at Wembley for an Oasis concert in 2025 (Image: Getty Images)

"But hosting events on this scale also brings very real pressures – from waste and street cleaning to enforcement, community safety and pressure on our public spaces. That's why it is so important we get the visitor levy right, so we can sustain that success while making sure our residents aren't left to shoulder an unfair share of the cost."

‌



The council leader added the levy "should not simply disappear into general budgets" believed money generated shouldn't just be used "to plug unrelated funding gaps in areas like adult social care or housing".

He also said the money should stay close to where it was generated, adding: "The money should be ringfenced for the visitor economy and the pressures that come with it – keeping streets clean, improving the public realm, enforcement and making the areas people come to visit better places to spend time in.

"For us, this is a pro-growth measure. We are asking visitors to make a small contribution, just as they do in many other major cities across Europe and investing that money back into the places they have come to visit.

‌



"If we invest more in the area around Wembley, keep it clean and make the public realm more attractive, visitors have a better experience. That encourages more people to come, means more money spent with local businesses and gives us more to invest back into the area. It becomes a virtuous circle, for a very modest contribution from visitors.”

"There is a question of trust here too. People are much more likely to understand a visitor levy if they can see where their money is going. If you stay in Brent and make a small contribution, you should be able to see that being reinvested in the place you have come to enjoy. Residents should be able to see that link as well."

Labour's 10 regional mayors, in a letter to the Chancellor and the Communities Secretary, committed to a 5% cap on any tourist tax introduced in their areas. They said: "Our underlying principle is that any levy we introduce should be modest and the revenue should be reinvested into areas which support our local economies."

Article continues below

Plans for the tax were first announced under Sir Keir Starmer following similar schemes introduced by the devolved administrations in Scotland and Wales. Prime Minister Andy Burnham reiterated his commitment to the scheme, framing it as part of his wider devolution agenda aimed at pushing power out of Whitehall.

Some industry chiefs shared their concerns over the plans and said they believe it could cost the UK hospitality and tourism sector as a whole as much as £1.6 billion. Allen Simpson, chief executive of UK Hospitality, said jobs could be at risk in communities that rely on tourism and hospitality.

Mr Simpson, speaking on BBC Radio 4, said: "I would say to those people in these communities that their jobs are now at risk. It will be the case that you’ll have holiday parks which can't open in the shoulder seasons and of course people who go on holiday will just have that little bit less money in their pocket."

News.title: Seven arrested as four men stabbed with one critical after stabbing in Bromley
News.content:
Seven arrested after four stabbed in Bromley High Street

Seven men have been arrested after four men were stabbed in an altercation on Bromley High Street, with one victim in a critical condition.

Seven arrested as four men stabbed with one critical after stabbing in Bromley

Seven men have been arrested after four men were stabbed during an altercation on Bromley High Street.

Police were called at around 2.15pm today, September 10, and attended alongside London Ambulance Service and London’s Air Ambulance.

Officers found four men with stab wounds. Three were taken to hospital with injuries described as non-life-threatening, while one man is in a critical condition.

All seven arrested men remain in custody as police enquiries continue. Officers said there is not believed to be any wider threat to the public.

A spokesperson for the London Ambulance Service said: "We were called at 2:19pm today (10 September) to reports of a stabbing on Bromley High Street, BR1.

“We sent ambulance crews, a paramedic in a fast response car, an incident response officer and an advanced paramedic. We also dispatched London’s Air Ambulance.

“We treated four patients at the scene and took them all to hospital”.

News.title: Mum put on child abuse register and given suspended sentence after letting son walk to pond
News.content:
Mum put on child abuse register and given suspended sentence after letting son walk to pond

Karyann Parkinson has left parents divided after being placed on the child abuse and neglect register for allowing her son, 5, to walk to a nature spot on his own from their home in Virginia

View 3 Images Parents are debating at what age a child should be allowed to walk on their own (stock photo) (Image: Getty Images)

A mother has sparked a parenting debate after she was arrested for allowing her five-year-old son to walk on his own to collect feathers near a pond.

‌



Mum-of-five Karyann Parkinson from Virginia has been handed a six-month suspended prison sentence and will remain on the child abuse and neglect registry for seven years after her lad Samuel was spotted on his own 800 meters from his home. She was charged with contributing to the delinquency of a minor, despite nothing happening to him, and was convicted by a judge after a trial in the Williamsburg Juvenile & Domestic Relations District Court.

‌



She was told if it happens again, she will go straight to jail. The treatment of Karyann has split many mums and dads after she allowed the boy to walk to the nature spot on his own, stressing that she could trust him - and that he was ready to show he could make the short trip without supervision.

‌



3 View 3 Images The mum was given a suspended jail sentence and placed on the child abuse and neglect registry (Image: Karyann Doty Parkinson/Facebook) 3 View 3 Images She let Samuel out on his own to collect goose feathers (Image: Karyann Doty Parkinson/Facebook)

She said that after the family went for a bike ride near their community pond, they made the short trip home. When they returned, Samuel asked if he could walk back and gather some more feathers - so the mum decided the time was right to see if he was ready to make a trip on his own.

But minutes later, the boy was stopped by a security guard, who alerted the police before Child Protective Services were called. Karyann told the authorities she hadn’t been breached any laws by allowing her son to walk on his own, but two weeks later she was charged - and is now is not allowed to volunteer at any of the schools her children attend.

‌



There is no official minimum legal age in the UK for a child to walk outside or walk to school on their own. The NSPCC state that kids usually start walking to school or outside independently between ages 9 to 11.

Karyann has spoken out to defend her parenting, and told Reason.com that her life was turned upside down just two weeks before the birth of her fifth child. She said: "Everyone in our neighborhood was close-knit and knew each other. There was 24-hour security, a 25-mph speed limit, sidewalks, and wide grass verges.

‌



"Sam was a responsible and independent kid. He'd made that journey hundreds of times with me, my husband, Dallin, 37, and our other children. Neglect occurs only when you put your child in serious or obvious danger, with no lower restriction on their age. Independence should be age-appropriate, taking into account the child's individual maturity and abilities."

As parents remain divided, she told Fox News: “I didn’t send him to play at the pond, I sent him down the path that happens to go past the pond to collect goose feathers. I know that a lot of people have seen the headlines and seen ‘five-year-old alone at a pond' - I think if I saw that in isolation, I’d probably be alarmed, too.

“We need to stop parenting from a place of fear and a place, you know, of obsessing over the unknown or some boogeyman who’s going to jump out from behind a bush.”

Article continues below

The mum says the family have filed an appeal because they want her case decided by a jury and are hopeful of hearing the outcome before Christmas.

News.title: At least 24 students dead after huge fire rips through two schools in DR Congo
News.content:
At least 24 students dead after huge fire rips through two schools in DR Congo

A massive fire has ripped through two schools and hundreds of other buildings in Bukavu, a city in the east of the Democrtic Republic of Congo with at least 24 children killed

View 4 Images A fire has ripped through buildings in Bukavu (Image: Xinhua/Shutterstock)

At least 24 children have been killed and many more injured in a stampede as they attempted to flee a fire ripping through two schools in Congo.

‌



Adults are also reported to have been killed with the death toll expected to rise following the fire in the highly populated Kadutu commune, in Bukavu, eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

‌



Lawrence Kanyuka, a spokesperson for the M23 rebel group which controls the city, said 19 girls and five boys were killed – adding that 29 people were being treated at local medical facilities.

‌



The fire started at a house before spreading to two adjoining schools and other buildings, said local neighbourhood administrator Moise Lubala, adding that several students were trapped inside Furaha secondary school and some suffocated.

View 4 Images At least 24 children have died from the fire in the city (Image: Xinhua/Shutterstock)

TUI flight forced into emergency landing at Cardiff Airport after engine bursts into flames READ MORE :

Six ways AI could make humans extinct in a horror digital doomsday READ MORE :

Around 300 houses have also been destroyed in the fire with the cause currently unknown.

‌



A mix of boys and girls of different ages, students at Furaha and at Ujamaa primary school, were brought to the Nyamulagira BDOM health centre in their school uniforms, said nurse Ciza Jean-Baptiste.

Medical staff were struggling to keep track of the exact number of injured because there were so many, he said. Images show children lying on the floor of the hospital in pain.

View 4 Images A person pictured going through the debris following the fire (Image: Xinhua/Shutterstock)

‌



“The exit was too narrow, so some students began jumping through windows while others rushed toward the door. As everyone tried to force their way out, students were pushed over and trampled on,” said Mr Lubala.

While the cause of the fire is not known, the neighbourhood where the fire started is densely populated and most houses are made out of wood, according to Mr Lubala.

DR Congo’s government struggles to exert control over the east of the country. M23 rebels, backed by Rwanda, took control of Bukavu in February 2025. More than 100 armed groups are vying for control of eastern DR Congo’s trillions of dollars in mineral wealth that is critical for much of the world ’s technology.

‌



View 4 Images It is feared that the death toll will rise following the fire (Image: AP Photo/Janvier Barhahiga)

Health services are under severe strain as the region grapples with the deadliest Ebola outbreak in history that has killed more than 3,300 people, with more than 6,800 confirmed cases recorded.

A statement has been released by the Congo government in Kinshasa which does not specify the numbers of casualties. "The Ministry of National Education and New Citizenship expressed deep sorrow over the deadly fire," it said.

Article continues below

"With several lives lost and many injured, the toll remains provisional. The minister offered condolences, affirmed solidarity with families, and ordered assessments of affected schools to ensure learning continuity."

News.title: Dad of teen killed in A66 crash charged with attacking mourner 'over comments made' at son's funeral
News.content:
Dad of teen killed in A66 crash charged with attacking mourner 'over comments made' at son's funeral

It has been claimed Gye Worthy, the father of 17-year-old crash victim Cole, allegedly took exception to comments made during his son's funeral service at Teesside Crematorium

View 4 Images Gye Worthy was arrested at his son Cole's funeral (Image: Facebook)

The father of one of the teenagers killed in the A66 crash has been charged with attacking a mourner at his son's funeral.

The remembrance ceremony for Cole Worthy, 17, was reduced to chaos when his father, Gye, 39, allegedly took exception to comments made during the service. He is accused of assaulting the mourner and of obstructing police who were called to deal with the disturbance.

A source close to the family said that Cole Worthy's mother Natalie McConnell had been "devastated and shocked" by the disruption to her son's memorial. Ms McConnell has long been separated from Gye Worthy and both now have new partners. A spokesman for Cleveland Police said Gye Worthy will face court next month.

4 View 4 Images Cole Worthy, right, was killed in the catastrophic crash last month 4 View 4 Images Police officers embrace before the funeral of PC Matthew Blades (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

In a statement the force said: "The 39-year-old man arrested yesterday (Wednesday 9 September) at Teesside Crematorium, following a disturbance during a service, has now been charged with common assault, public order and obstructing police. He is due to appear before Teesside Magistrates’ Court on 2nd October."

Sarah Moloney, a friend of Ms McConnell, thanked mourners for their attendance on her behalf. In a social media post she said: "To everyone who came today for our Coley, thank you from the very bottom of our hearts.

View 4 Images A house in Ruskin Avenue, Middlesbrough, after being rammed by a car (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

"Seeing so many faces who loved him cared for him and held him close means more than we can ever put into words, your presence your hugs your kind words and every beautiful memory you shared. Cole was so loved and today showed us just how far that love reached.

"Thank you for walking this hard day with us, thank you for loving him, for remembering him and for being here for us He will live on in all our hearts forever. Rest peacefully our beautiful Coley, we love you more than anything."

Gye Worthy, from Acklam, Middlesbrough, works as an offshore deck foreman and is the boss of his own specialist lifting company which operates on offshore platforms. His semi detached £200,000 home recently suffered serious damage in a criminal act currently under investigation by Cleveland Police.

Cole Worthy was killed within minutes of his father's home being attacked, alongside four of his associates and two police officers, PC Matthew Blades, 37 and PC Tom Clough, 38. They were all killed at 3.39am on Saturday August 22 when the police armed response vehicle was struck at South Bank, near Middlesbrough, by a speeding VW Passat containing the five youths and young men aged between 17 and 23.

Worthy, Jakub Matusiak, 23, Makai Saddington, 18, Michael Cahill, 23, and Theo Rae, 17, were also killed in the smash. Police said the five all had links to organised crime and had been trying to flee police when they drove the wrong way up the A66 into the police vehicle.

The incident was blamed on a tit for tat gangland turf war over the supply of drugs on Teesside. PCs Clough and Blades died from severe head and neck injuries at the scene.

The final funeral of the five youths in the Passat was also taking place today in County Durham as family gathered to mark the death of Michael Cahill. At an earlier vigil held in his honour, a number of cars - including a £80,000 Porsche - were driven at speed around a field at Haswell, near Peterlee, and set ablaze.

News.title: Married At First Sight star dies aged 39 after brain tumour battle
News.content:
Married At First Sight star dies aged 39 after brain tumour battle

Married at First Sight star Adrian Szymaniak, who found fame on the show in 2018, has died at the age of 39 following a year-long battle with an aggressive form of brain cancer

View 5 Images Married at First Sight star Adrian Szymaniak has died at the age of 39 (Image: JamPress)

Married at First Sight star Adrian Szymaniak has died at the age of 39.

‌



The TV star, who found fame when he met and married Anita on the set of the Polish version of Channel 4's hit romance experiment, was diagnosed with grade four glioblastoma, the most aggressive form of brain cancer, in July 2025.

‌



Anita took to social media to share the sad news, writing on Instagram: "It is with great sorrow that we announce that Adrian has passed away. In these extremely difficult moments, the most important things for us are silence, closeness and the ability to say goodbye to Him with our loved ones."

‌



5 View 5 Images Anita asked for pricacy at this said time (Image: JamPress) 5 View 5 Images The couple married on the Polish version of the hit show in 2018 (Image: JamPress)

Following their 2018 wedding, the couple went on to have two children together and Anita concluded her post by asking followers to respect her privacy at this time.

She added: '"Adrian's funeral will be family and private only. We need now, above all, the peace and space, to say goodbye to Adrian with love, dignity and silence. We thank everyone who respects our will, privacy and this particularly difficult time for us.

‌



"At this extremely difficult time for us, we also ask you to refrain from sending personal condolences, calls and messages. We need silence, peace and space to live this time with our loved ones.

"Thank you for understanding, respecting and respecting our need for privacy. Adrian's Wife, Children, and Friends." According to reports, Adrian's funeral took place on Wednesday in Żołędowo. Close friend Piotr Kęsik said: "Today we say goodbye to a good man. Adrian was joyful, honest, cheerful, loyal. I want to cry, but he probably wouldn’t have wanted that."

5 View 5 Images The pair went on to have two children together (Image: JamPress) 5 View 5 Images When he was alive, Adrian said he shared his story to give others 'hope' (Image: JamPress)

‌



Adrian underwent several rounds of treatment amid his cancer battle, and wrote on Instagram in an emotional post: "I share my story because I have no other options, but also because I believe it can give someone hope.

"Instead of the daily sadness and regret, I choose to be grateful for every day. Instead of being helpless, I choose to fight and plan for the future.

"One day I have plenty of strength. Another I don't have any. This is what an illness looks like. It's not just lying in bed, it's also laughter and joy, sometimes even with much smaller things than before. Let the smile be on your faces as often as possible."

Article continues below

The Polish version of Married At First Sight, titled Ślub od pierwszego wejrzenia, has aired on the TVN channel since 2016. It is one of several iterations of the experimental format, which sees strangers "marry" after being matched by a panel of experts.
