Sports.title: Baseball icon and Hiroshima atomic bomb survivor Isao Harimoto dies aged 86
Sports.content:
Baseball icon and Hiroshima atomic bomb survivor Isao Harimoto dies aged 86

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Baseball legend Isao Harimoto, who survived the atomic bombing of Hiroshima, has died aged 86.

The Korean-Japanese icon, who was born in Hiroshima in 1940 to Korean parents who migrated to Japan during the country's rule of Korea, died in Tokyo on Wednesday.

Growing up, he overcame huge adversity as a child. Firstly he was involved in an accident in 1944 that left him with severe burns on his right hand.

The result of that left him with limited mobility in his thumb and forefinger, while his middle three fingers became permanently curled.

Then a year later, he survived the United States of America's atomic bombing of Hiroshima during World War II on August 6, 1945.

Harimoto, whose birth name was Jang Hun, survived after his mother used her body to shield him and one of his sisters from the blast. However, sadly another sister did not survive. Between 60,000 and 80,000 people were killed instantly - with the final death toll calculated at 135,000.

Korean-Japanese baseball legend Isao Harimoto died aged 86 in Tokyo on Wednesday

Known as the 'Hit Machine' he recorded the most hits in Japanese baseball history at 3,085

After a difficult childhood, Harimoto later turned his attention to baseball. He had to learn to play left-handed due to his injuries and wore a custom glove to fit his injured right hand that allowed him to catch the ball.

But despite those hindrances, Harimoto enjoyed a distinguished 23-year career - playing for Toei Flyers, the Yomiuri Giants and the Lotte Orions across his homeland. At the Flyers he helped them win their first Japan Series in 1962.

Known as the 'Hit Machine' he recorded the most hits in Japanese baseball history at 3,085 and is the only player in Nippon Professional Baseball League (NPB) to surpass the 3,000 landmark.

Furthermore he is the only player in NPB history to hit over 500 home runs and steal more than 300 bases - with his figures at 504 and 319 respectively. By comparison, only three players in Major League Baseball history have achieved the same feat in Barry Bonds, Willie Mays and Alex Rodriguez.

An 18-time All-Star, he was inducted into the Japanese Baseball Hall of Fame in 1990.

The Golden Players Club, one of Japan’s two halls of fame, wrote: 'All members of the Meikyukai express our deep respect and gratitude for Mr Isao Harimoto’s many years of great achievements, and we sincerely pray [following] his passing.'

Sports.title: Alexis Mac Allister learns his lesson after public revelation over his Liverpool future - more of these destructive winners and there will be a new contract in front of him, writes IAN LADYMAN
Sports.content:
Alexis Mac Allister is a World Cup champion and Premier League winner but even the most experienced footballers occasionally learn lessons. The Liverpool midfielder this week learnt that maybe it’s best to earn new contracts by winning matches rather than lighting up press conferences. Mac Allister’s decision to preface this game by moaning about the lack of a new contract offer was either clumsy or sinister in its timing. Only he knows his motive but what is certain is his manager Andoni Iraola – only three meaningful games into his Anfield tenure – could have done without it. But here, out on the grass where it really mattered, Mac Allister rescued an important European game against a high calibre opponent with a 20-yard shot so pure and powerful and destructive that it may as well have been accompanied by the crashing of cymbals and the banging of drums. Much more of that and there will indeed be a piece of paper in front of the Argentinean with his name on it and maybe a 27-year-old footballer of great experience will reflect on that over time. Liverpool needed the goal, too. Unconvincing early on against Diego Simeone’s streetwise side, Liverpool had fallen behind to a Marcos Llorente goal after 17 minutes. Liverpool came from behind to beat Atletico Madrid 2-1 in their Champions League opener Alexis Mac Allister scored the winner, a day after he cast doubt over his Liverpool future Andoni Iraola picked up a victory in his first game as a manger in the Champions League And though Dominik Szoboszlai had equalised just before half-time, the game was very much in the balance before Mac Allister delivered so sweetly at the Kop End. This had felt like the biggest test of Liverpool’s early season beforehand and that was how it turned out. Atletico have not started the Spanish league season particularly impressively but they were familiar in much of what they did here. When Llorente gave them the lead in the 17th minute, it was his fifth goal against Liverpool – exactly half his total Champions League tally – and that pretty much summed things up at that stage. Atletico were sharp and hungry and as irritatingly sly as ever. It felt at times as though they were rolling out a blueprint with which to thwart Liverpool that had been well drilled through the years. Patience is certainly a virtue when a team plays a Simeone side. They will give you nothing and try and take plenty, especially when the referee isn’t looking. For a while they were too comfortable here and it took Szoboszlai’s goal just before half-time to settle Iraola’s team down a little. After that, doubtless to Iraola’s relief, it was a different game. The new Liverpool manager - in charge of his first Champions League game – had handed £125m Bradley Barcola his first start and asked young Rio Ngumoha to play on the other side after Cody Gakpo reported with a minor injury. Liverpool could have scored within 15 seconds. Szoboszlai robbed an opponent straight from the kick-off and played Alexander Isak in down the right only for the Swede to pull his right foot shot across goal and wide. It was a really good chance but didn’t immediately serve to preface more of the same. Instead it was Atletico who carried the first half threat, looking to penetrate Liverpool’s dreadfully square back four whenever they broke through the centre of the field. Iraola had stuck with the same full-backs who had started last Friday’s win at Ipswich. Both were to feature in Liverpool’s equaliser but left-back Milos Kerkez was all over the place for the first half an hour. He often is. Kerkez, once a Bournemouth player for Iraola, seems to do everything at 100 miles an hour and as such hardly ever looks in control. Either going forward or in retreat, the Hungarian injects chaos in this Liverpool team and at some point he is going to have to learn. Here, he was a yard behind his defensive team-mates as Julian Alvarez played Llorente through towards the Kop for the Spaniard to lift the ball over Alisson Becker and into the goal with ease. Atletico were worth their lead at this point and Liverpool’s immediate response was unconvincing. They were slow and clunky with the ball and – with their best defensive midfielder Ryan Gravenberch inexplicably left on the bench yet again - as open as a barn door when they were without it. Marcos Llorente had put Atletico 1-0 ahead to continue his superb record against Liverpool Dominik Szoboszlai equalised before half-time, and Mac Allister's had a decisive intervention Bradley Barcola made his European bow for the Reds on what was his first start for the club Alisson saved well from Alvarez when Atletico caught the Liverpool defence square again in the 27th minute and only in the ten minutes before half-time did the home team start to deliver any kind of momentum and threat. Atletico goalkeeper Jan Oblak saved well from Florian Wirtz after Isak’s superb far post pass before Kerkez showed great heart to win the ball in midfield and set in motion the move that led to the equaliser. His pass across the penalty area allowed Barcola to shoot and when the ball ran loose off the goalkeeper, right-back Ronald Araujo had advanced to flick it cleverly to Szoboszlai who side footed it gently into the corner. Simeone’s team came again as Alex Baena volleyed wide but at the start of the second half it was Liverpool who found a rhythm. Barcola should have scored his first Liverpool goal – shooting wide after Wirtz played him clear – but soon after Mac Allister slammed in his redemption goal from 20 yards after Ngumoha’s run across the byline preceded a hurried clearance from a Spanish defence feeling the squeeze for the first time. The adrenaline rush of a deficit being turned into a lead in the space of ten minutes was significant and almost tangible. It didn’t herald further Liverpool dominance, though. Indeed it was Alvarez who spurned the next chance of the game, side footing at Alisson when he should have done better from 14 yards. By now Barcola had gone off with what Liverpool will hope was only cramp. With fifteen minutes left, it was Atletico who were once again pushing. In vain, as it turned out. This felt big for Liverpool and their manager. And maybe for Alexis Mac Allister too.

Sports.title: Dan Lawrence says Ollie Robinson is 'at the peak of his powers' after England bowler continues remarkable series against Pakistan - and gives verdict on own position in team
Sports.content:
Ollie Robinson is operating at the ‘peak of his powers’ and making his England team-mates believe he will take a wicket every ball.

That was the assessment from the slip cordon of Dan Lawrence, after Robinson struck twice in the opening over of Pakistan’s second innings at Edgbaston.

‘When he's bowling, when he's putting it in the same spot pretty much every ball, you certainly do feel in the game behind the stumps, especially when you've got someone pretty much at the peak of his powers,’ said Lawrence.

Robinson’s double strike took his series wickets tally to an astonishing 21 at a cost of just 6.66 runs each.

Bad weather ended play prematurely, leaving a Pakistan team yet to make 200 in five previous innings on 52 for two and requiring 268 more runs to make Joe Root’s England bat again.

At the other end of the day, Surrey’s Lawrence dominated the early scoring in a rapid start alongside Harry Brook, but like his fifth-wicket partner failed to turn a half century into a hundred, finishing with 65 off 82 balls, in a score of 453.

Dan Lawrence heaped praise on Ollie Robinson after he continued his remarkable series

Lawrence, who earlier scored 65, said the England bowler was 'at the peak of his powers'

With three 50s in four innings, the 29-year-old might have done enough to maintain his place in the squad for the winter tour of South Africa. Jacob Bethell will be back from knee surgery by then and Sam Curran has been nominated as Ben Stokes’ successor in the all-rounder role. The rest will be determined over the next fortnight.

Incoming coach Stephen Fleming is scheduled to arrive next week and is understood to be keen on getting around the country, talking to directors of cricket and coaches about the country’s leading players.

‘In regards to position in the team, only the selectors and the captain will know that, and I'm pretty happy with how I've contributed and we'll see what happens,’ Lawrence said.

‘I felt like I was playing really nicely and it was a really good surface to bat on against a tiring attack. I thought I was going to make a really big score to be honest, but it wasn't meant to be.’

Surrey team-mate Jamie Smith and Robinson also made half centuries, although the former was unable to take his place behind the stumps due to a dislocated finger.

Jordan Cox will keep wicket for the remainder of a contest that appears destined to finish on Friday, marking the beginning of the post-Bazball era with a 3-0 whitewash.

Sports.title: Pakistan endure another day of despair as miserable tour continues: This once great cricketing nation has been reduced to chaos and cluelessness as England close in on series whitewash, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH
Sports.content:
Moments after Ollie Robinson, immovable from the crest of his wave, had Saim Ayub caught in the slips by Harry Brook from the first ball of Pakistan’s second innings, a PA announcement warned Edgbaston stewards of a ‘Code Red’.

It had apparently been triggered by a fire alarm and, for a few seconds, the crowd fell eerily silent. But they burst into life three balls later when Robinson had Abdullah Shafique poking low to Joe Root at first slip, leaving the tourists nought for two and facing a Code Red situation of their own.

The fire alarm proved false, and Pakistan saved at least a little face by reaching 52 for two before rain ended play shortly after 5pm.

But as Root’s team closed in on a 3–0 whitewash in gloomy Birmingham, it was possible to feel two emotions at the same time: delight for England, who batted with panache and bowled with precision, and despair for Pakistan, a once great side reduced to chaos and cluelessness by the machinations of their board and the misery of their players.

There was uproar in Karachi and Lahore when, only two days into this series, their side were described as the worst their country had sent to these shores for 50 years. Those voices have fallen silent now, with England – in disarray themselves not long ago – largely doing as they pleased on the second day of this third and final Test.

Resuming on 156 for four, they thrashed 297 in 60 overs before being dismissed for 453, at which point Robinson took his series haul to 21 wickets at an average of 6.66 with the kind of precision that turns metronomes green with envy. It has all been closer to bloodsport than sport.

Ollie Robinson shone again as England closed in on a series whitewash over Pakistan

It was another day of despair for Pakistan as their miserable tour of England nears an end

We should be careful what we wish for, of course. Until recently, the idea of England winning every Test of a series would have been greeted with a snort of derision. But while they deserve credit for keeping their foot on Pakistan’s throat, the one-sidedness of the cricket has raised more questions about a format that rarely stops fretting over its future.

It’s no good grumbling about the unfettered growth of the T20 franchise circuit when Test cricket is properly contested by only a handful of nations. And it’s no good wondering why this inequality has been allowed to arise when the bigger nations shrug their shoulders at the ICC’s lopsided financial model, and the ICC themselves turn a blind eye to the game’s growing politicisation.

As this tour has confirmed, Pakistan are on the wrong side of each of these debates, with the chairman of their cricket board, Mohsin Naqvi, doubling up as the country’s interior minister, and presiding over the farcical culling of almost half their squad between Lord’s and Edgbaston.

It all meant the day proceeded along predictable lines, with Harry Brook and Dan Lawrence sniffing out any prospect of a Pakistani comeback by taking 73 from the morning’s first 10 overs while barely breaking sweat.

But if there has been one criticism of England, it has been the failure of their batsmen to convert starts into something more meaningful, and here again they promised more than they delivered.

Brook had struck the perfect tempo in moving to 75 in three and a quarter hours when he pushed an off-break from Ayub towards midwicket and set off for a single even as Shan Masood swooped on the ball, before running him out comfortably at the non-striker’s end.

Might Lawrence reach three figures instead? Moments before lunch, he contrived to chop a widish delivery from Mohammad Imran on to his stumps, and walked off in anguish for 65. Three half-centuries in four innings since his recall have been a good return, but the battle for top-six places is cranking up. This was an opportunity missed.

Jamie Smith, batting with a dislocated left index finger sustained in the field on the first day, played some meaty strokes for his third sixty in five innings, only to provide a simple return catch off a leading edge to Razaullah.

And while Robinson hit out for his second Test fifty, his dismissal left England with 21 half-centuries from six games this summer, and a lone hundred, by Ben Duckett against New Zealand at Trent Bridge.

Unless one of Pakistan’s batsmen can go big tomorrow, this will be the first Test series in England of three matches or more not to feature an individual century since the 1888 Ashes.

Harry Brook and Dan Lawrence were two of five England batsmen to pass 50 in their innings

This Pakistan side are one of the worst touring teams to ever come to here for a Test series

Not that any of this troubled Robinson as he performed his now customary demolition of Pakistan’s top order.

Ayub’s most recent cricket had been for Jamaica Kingsmen in the Caribbean Premier League, which most sensible set-ups might think was no kind of preparation for red-ball cricket under grey English skies. Sure enough, he completed a pair by wafting hopelessly at his first ball.

Cox, keeping in place of the injured Smith, now came up to the stumps for Shafique, who poked at Robinson as if in a trance. Since making 61 at Headingley, Shafique has managed 23 in five innings, and been dismissed in five of his six by Robinson.

Duckett put down a slip catch for the third time in the game when Shan Masood flashed at the luckless Gus Atkinson, while Jofra Archer lacked his usual menace. But such is the gulf between the sides that England can afford these blemishes and still win this game at a canter.

Sports.title: Boxing Day bonanza is back with SEVEN games as Premier League confirm TV dates for festive period - following last season's backlash with just one fixture played
Sports.content:
The Premier League has confirmed that seven games will be staged on Boxing Day after releasing its latest set of fixtures. Four games will be held at 3pm, with Aston Villa facing Leeds at 12.30pm, Hull taking on Liverpool at 5.30pm, before Newcastle host Manchester City at 8pm. A triple header follows on Super Sunday on Sky Sports on December 27, with Chelsea facing Coventry at 2pm, Man United hosting Nottingham Forest at 4.30pm and Crystal Palace taking on champions Arsenal at 7pm. It comes after the league faced widespread backlash after hosting just one game on Boxing Day - one of the most popular dates on the football calendar - last year. That will kick off a busy schedule over the festive season, with three further rounds of matches to be held over the period up to January 7. A round of midweek evening fixtures will take place on December 29 and December 30, before Leeds host Everton in the only game on New Year's Day. Boxing Day football is back in the Premier League with seven fixtures confirmed Last year, Man United vs Newcastle was the only fixture that was scheduled on Boxing Day The rest of that gameweek will take place on January 2 and January 3, before the festive schedule concludes with a round of games that will fall from January 5 to January 7. Every fixture from the December 29 to December 30 round and the one from January 5 to January 7 will be broadcast on Sky Sports The early announcement comes after the Premier League consulted broadcast partners, the Football Supporters' Association and representatives from club Fan Advisory Boards. There is a desire to give as much notice as possible for those travelling to games. As part of the schedule, each club is guaranteed at least a 60-hour break between matches in order to help them deal with the fixture congestion. The early announcement is likely to be welcomed by fans after the Premier League was heavily criticised for arranging just one game on Boxing Day last season. Manchester United vs Newcastle was the only match, with the top flight blaming scheduling issues caused by European football and the Carabao Cup. At the time, they said: 'There are now several challenges to Premier League fixture scheduling rooted in the expansion of European club competitions – which led to a revision of our domestic calendar ahead of last season, including changes to the FA Cup. 'This ultimately left the Premier League as a 33-weekend competition – fewer than previous seasons, despite being a 380-match competition since 1995. 'With fewer weekends to work with, the league is bound by how the calendar falls. 'The league can give an assurance that next season there will be more Premier League matches on Boxing Day – as the date falls on a Saturday.'

Sports.title: Chelsea Confidential: Marco Palestra injury update revealed, scouting blow for Blues, Xabi Alonso's view on the Declan Rice 'foul', club's stance on Mauricio Pochettino title talk and latest on missing Geovany Quenda
Sports.content:
Marco Palestra is getting closer to his Premier League debut after this week taking part in individual training with one of Xabi Alonso’s coaches at Cobham, Confidential can reveal.

That was a precursor to participating in Chelsea’s main sessions which would be the final step before being passed fit for selection. Alonso is keen to have him available, but learned his lesson when rushing back Moises Caicedo, who reinjured himself upon returning two weekends ago.

The manager has been preaching caution with both Palestra and Caicedo since that setback, with the Blues boss insisting he will only use the pair once he believes it does not represent a risk. Before the September international break, Chelsea have Hull at home and Brentford away.

Chelsea signed Palestra for £47million from Atalanta. He was named Serie A Defender of the Year while on loan at Cagliari last season, where he was named the fastest player in the division.

The 21-year-old Italian seems set to play an important role under Alonso after the wing back and full back was a feature throughout pre-season, starting in friendlies against Tottenham, Juventus, AC Milan and Real Sociedad.

However, Palestra was then missing from the first matchday squad that won 3-2 at Fulham and has not been seen since, including in Wednesday night's Carabao Cup clash with Leeds. Alonso said he picked up his problem in training a few days prior to travelling to Craven Cottage.

With sources saying Palestra is now involved in outdoor work, he appears to be nearing availability. Confidential asked Alonso earlier this week whether Caicedo was training, and Chelsea’s manager said he was, so the midfielder is likewise closing in on his own return.

Marco Palestra is getting closer to his Premier League debut with Chelsea after this week taking part in individual training, Confidential can reveal

Chelsea midfielder Moises Caicedo is likewise closing in on a return

CHELSEA LOSE SCOUT TO ADARABIOYO AGENCY

One of Chelsea’s leading scouts, Stewart Thompson, has left the club and joined the football agency, WNRS, headed up by Gbolahan Adarabioyo, the brother of Tosin. Thompson made the move to Chelsea as a first-team scout in 2023. Prior to that, he had been a UK and European scout for Manchester City since 2010.

WNRS handled Tosin’s switch to Tottenham on deadline day. That was understood to be worth an initial £10m with a further £2m in add-ons for Chelsea.

Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi was said to play a pivotal role in that signing, along with securing Mykhailo Mudryk on a season-long loan with a £75m option to buy. In a blow to Tottenham, Mudryk has suffered an ankle injury in training and is set to be sidelined for several weeks.

Meanwhile, Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli, the 16-year-old academy prodigy who impressed on Chelsea’s pre-season tour of Australia and Asia, has also joined WNRS. The agency’s tagline is: ‘Football management – built for winners.’

Chelsea's Mykhailo Mudryk, who is on a season-long loan at Spurs, has suffered an ankle injury in training and is set to be sidelined for several weeks

ALONSO TURNS QUESTIONER

In between asking Alonso about free agents and Caicedo earlier this week at Cobham, Confidential wanted to know the Chelsea manager's thoughts on Morgan Rogers’ reaction when he shoved Declan Rice in their 2-1 loss to Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium.

Whether he liked his player showing such passion. Whether he would have preferred his £117m summer signing to have kept a cool head. Alonso did answer, but only once he had asked Confidential a couple of his own questions first. Here’s how our exchange went:

CONFIDENTIAL: ‘Rogers got a yellow for shoving Rice – do you like that passion or would you rather he did not react?’

ALONSO: ‘Did you see the tackle?’

CONFIDENTIAL: ‘I did.’

ALONSO: ‘And?'

CONFIDENTIAL: ‘And Rice should have been the one booked with a Chelsea free-kick for the trip.’

ALONSO: ‘It was clear. It was pretty clear. It’s the emotion of the game. Sometimes, to be able to manage all of them, it’s difficult. We were trying to find the equaliser. Morgan saw the chance to get into the box. It was a tackle that was very… I don’t know how to say in English…’

CONFIDENTIAL: ‘Cynical?’

ALONSO: ‘Cynical – that’s a good one. He showed his frustration. But it’s part of the game.’

Morgan Rogers shows his frustration with Declan Rice after the Arsenal man's 'cynical' foul

CAS: NO CHELSEA CONTACT

Confidential checked in with the Court of Arbitration for Sport, who say there has been no request from Chelsea concerning how they missed out on signing Lamine Camara from Monaco on deadline day.

We have not heard of any desire to try to escalate that situation into a legal matter, either.

Chelsea remain disappointed with Monaco for how they pulled the plug on that £47m deal, but the noise coming back from inside Stamford Bridge is that they are moving on from what happened.

POCH: STRIP CHELSEA OF THE TITLE

If there was any doubt left within Chelsea that they should not have hired a head coach whose heart was still with Tottenham, Mauricio Pochettino may have just wiped that away.

In an hour-long interview conducted in London with various newspapers, Pochettino, now in charge of the United States, said Chelsea should be stripped of their 2017 Premier League title and that it should be awarded to Tottenham, who finished second that season.

That follows Chelsea being fined £10m this summer for breaching rules relating to payments to agents between 2009 and 2022. The club escaped sporting and retrospective sanctions.

Other than some raised eyebrows, it does not appear there will be an official response to Pochettino’s comments from Chelsea.

Pochettino, now in charge of the US national team, said Chelsea should be stripped of their 2017 Premier League title

GRAHAM POTTER AND THE PHILOSOPHER’S MOAN

Speaking of former Chelsea managers having a pop…

Graham Potter is currently the head coach of the Swedish national team and has been using his Instagram for some sly digs at his old club. The former Chelsea and West Ham boss was surprisingly frank after he uploaded some snaps of himself trying Pilates.

When one user commented: ‘Hopefully you are better at Pilates than you are a football manager.’

Potter replied: ‘I’ll try not to do Pilates in a dysfunctional place and I will be OK.’

When another user responded: 'Didn’t mind the money though, did you?’

Potter replied: ‘Absolutely not.’

They were West Ham fans to whom he was replying, so maybe he will still be welcomed back at Stamford Bridge should he ever want to survey a Swedish player for his national team.

Graham Potter tries a spot of Pilates - and posts it on his Instagram feed

And he was surprisingly frank in an the exchange with a West Ham fan that followed

GEORGE-OUS SAVING

Everton’s deal to sign Tyrique George was worth £24m – £18m plus £6m in add-ons – while Chelsea will retain a 15 per cent sell-on fee for any future sale.

It is already looking like a bargain from Everton’s perspective. Not only because of the 20-year-old’s goal against Manchester United at the weekend, but he can also help David Moyes with his striker shortage, having been used up front at Chelsea.

CHANCE FOR PAEZ TO GET BACK ON TRACK

There was considerable excitement before Kendry Paez arrived.

Chelsea secured him from Independiente del Valle in Ecuador on a pre-agreement worth £17.3m when he was 16 years old, and he arrived once 18. However, loans with sister side Strasbourg and Argentinian club River Plate did not go to plan amid speculation surrounding his lifestyle.

Chelsea tried to find him an English club to join on loan until the end of the summer but they were unable to do so. Now, he is 19, somewhat stuck, and not in Alonso’s first-team plans.

What it does give Paez is the chance to work with Chelsea staff for a few months at least, and hopefully that can do him some good. In the last two years, this South American teenager has lived in Ecuador, France, Argentina and England.

It has been a chaotic time for him, and hopefully he can use this period to focus on getting his once-promising career back on track.

Kendry Paez, 19, has been here, there and everywhere since joining Chelsea but is now with the club for a spell and can hopefully knuckle down

PANEL TO REVEAL GABRIEL VERDICT

The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents panel sit down each week to review the major refereeing decisions from every weekend, delivering a verdict on whether calls were right or wrong.

Previously, the results remained private, used only to tell Howard Webb’s organisation where their officials were in the wrong. As of this season, they are being made public.

That means by this time next week, we should know whether this panel believe Arsenal centre back Gabriel should have been in bother for kicking Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez in the head during that Premier League showdown at the Emirates.

There are certainly some within Chelsea who think Gabriel got away with one. Alonso was asked for his take on the Gabriel-Martinez incident, but he said with a little smile at the end of his answer: ‘I have my opinion but we’ll leave it there.’

Arsenal's Gabriel kicks Chelsea keeper Emi Martinez in the head at the Emirates last weekend - but he escaped punishment

QUENDA ABSENCE – A TECHNICAL DECISION

Geovany Quenda was an unused substitute in the Carabao Cup against Leeds, having only appeared once in all competitions all season, coming on in the 82nd minute at Fulham in Chelsea’s first Premier League match of the campaign.

Sources close to Quenda say he is not carrying any injury, and that he is fully fit.

It appears, therefore, it is simply down to technical decisions that Alonso is not using the 19-year-old winger and wing back who arrived from Sporting CP this summer. Chelsea spent £40m to acquire him on a pre-agreement.

Sports.title: Musical Times storms to the head of the betting for next year's 1,000 Guineas with scintillating display... plus our top tips for Day Two of the St Leger Festival
Sports.content:
Musical Times storms to the head of the betting for next year's 1,000 Guineas with scintillating display... plus our top tips for Day Two of the St Leger Festival

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Musical Times stormed to the head of the betting for next year's 1,000 Guineas with a scintillating display in the Group 2 Betfred May Hill Stakes at Doncaster.

A smooth winner of her first two starts at Newmarket and Yarmouth, the daughter of Lope De Vega travelled kindly in the hands of rider William Buick before being asked to quicken at the furlong marker.

From that point, the response was instantaneous as the 7/4 favourite shot clear of her toiling rivals to score geared down by an enormous seven-and-a-half length margin from Scommessa Sicura and go one better than her mother, Dubai Fountain, who was runner-up in the Group 2 contest.

Bookmakers William Hill reacted by slashing Godolphin's unbeaten filly to 6/1 favourite (from 25/1) for next May's Betfred 1,000 Guineas, while the Leeds-based firm installed Musical Times as 7/4 market leader for the bet365 Fillies' Mile at Newmarket on October 9.

'We'll head to the Fillies' Mile, which was always our plan since Yarmouth really,' reported a delighted Appleby who was saddling his sixth winner from nine September runners.

'She's handled that slightly slower ground today but she's a neat filly, so if it came up quick at Newmarket in the autumn or in the spring it wouldn't worry me.'

Musical Times streaks to victory in the highlight of day one of the St Leger Festival

SAM'S TOP TIPS FOR DAY TWO 2.25 – Final Objective (ew): The talented Pershaada should relish tackling her own age group after taking on the likes of the trail-blazing Bacio in a warm renewal of the Nunthorpe Stakes at York last time. However, the prospect of easy ground will demand a different skillset from the speedy filly and Final Objective could trouble the likely favourite now he drops to the minimum trip for the first time. The selection posted a clear career best in the Group 2 Gimcrack Stakes at York and a strongly-run five furlongs could see him to good effect. 4.45 – Launch Sequence: The application of the first-time cheekpieces and the return to six furlongs could see Launch Sequence power to a first career success in this competitive nursery. A promising debut over course and distance has been followed by two highly promising efforts in decent company with his creditable effort in the Convivial Maiden at York enhanced when the runner-up was placed in Group company next time out. 5.20 - Something Splendid (e/w): It is quite a while since Peter Chapple-Hyam was enjoying Classic success, but the ardent West Bromwich Albion fan has sent out a couple of winners in recent days and Something Splendid is fancied to defy a 5lb penalty for a recent Yarmouth triumph. No doubt buoyed by his beloved team's start to the new Championship season, the Newmarket handler saw the son of Postponed finish runner-up in a division of this corresponding race last year and, although he was later awarded the race when the winner was thrown out, the selection can win this year's renewal under his own volition today.

The Newmarket handler saddled Desert Flower to win the Fillies' Mile before winning the 1,000 Guineas two years ago, but was at pains to point out she was a different model to Musical Times.

'I don't see why she (Musical Times) shouldn't be a Guineas filly. We won this a couple of years ago with Desert Flower, who went on to win the Guineas.

'Funnily enough I see this filly as more of a Guineas filly than Desert Flower, who was big and scopey and unfortunately didn't quite win the Oaks.'

Waardah was another of the fairer sex to shine on Town Moor, comfortably capturing the Group 2 Betfred Park Hill Fillies' Stakes for trainer Owen Burrows and rider Callum Rodriguez.

'We haven't seen a lot of her as she does appreciate a bit of juice in the ground,' said Burrows.

'It was a good run at Carlisle against David O'Meara's Group 1 filly (Estrange) and she was only beaten a neck at Goodwood on quick ground last time, so I was hopeful today.

'She's in the fillies' race (Prix de Royallieu) in France on Arc weekend so that would be her next target and, depending on how that went, we'd have a look at the Group 1 Fillies & Mares on British Champions Day at Ascot.'

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
